findings.text: A caller supplied descriptor can be initialized from a memory range plus a mode selector, with kernel mode deriving width from build configuration and other modes deriving it from the requested 64-bit selection. Length acquisition is then attempted; its failure propagates, full acquisition reports success, and partial acquisition reports invalid argument. Completeness requires opcode, ModRM, SIB, displacement and immediate groups all to be marked acquired.

Opcode acquisition is idempotent once marked complete and otherwise requires prefix acquisition first. One acquisition path handles vector extensions by consulting map and prefix selectors and rejecting encodings that demand a different vector form or fail acceptance, with a narrow operand width adjustment for scalable encodings lacking a width indication. A second path handles the two byte REX form by selecting plain or escaped attribute lookup according to its map indicator. The legacy path preserves only the invalid in 64-bit marker for prohibited encodings, follows escape links using the most recent prefix identity, and rejects encodings demanding vector form. Success marks the opcode acquired.

Several attribute queries are pure flag membership tests over an attribute word, distinguishing escape encodings, encodings restricted to vector forms, scalable vector encodings, and encodings invalid in 64-bit mode. A companion selector derives a small escape table index by masking and shifting the attribute word.

The extended REX form is recognized by a two byte length of its prefix field, and its map selection is carried in the top bit of the trailing byte. The extension flags for register, index and base fields are each carried in a distinct low bit of the same trailing byte value.

Vector prefix length distinguishes compact, standard and extended forms, with the extended form recognized by a four byte length. Map selection occupies the low three bits of the relevant extended prefix byte, while standard vector and external operation map selections each occupy the low five bits of their respective bytes. The scaled index selector occupies the middle three bits of its addressing byte. Accessors for short prefixes yield zero rather than reading absent bytes, including the width flag when fewer than three prefix bytes are present.

Attribute lookup consults master tables first and selects variant tables only under prefix and grouping conditions, returning absence when an index is out of range or a table pointer is missing. Escape lookup keys on escape identity plus last prefix identity when the master entry admits variants. Vector lookup keys on map and prefix selectors unless the master entry denotes a group or no prefix selector is present. External operation lookup adjusts the map selector by its minimum before indexing.

Trailing address and immediate capture support two, four and eight byte width selections. Two byte selection fills a single narrow field, four byte selection fills a single wider field, and eight byte selection splits across paired first and second fields marked jointly acquired, except far pointer capture which has no eight byte form and otherwise appends a two byte selector. Any other width fails.

Confidential guest fault handling selects a user or kernel instruction fetch path based on privilege context and firmware memory identity, then decodes fetched bytes in 64-bit mode within a bounded temporary buffer. Kernel fetch failure synthesizes instruction fetch page fault information anchored at the faulting instruction pointer, decode failure yields a dedicated decode failed outcome, and success yields an okay outcome.

Guest memory emulation performs accesses through unchecked user accessors that report failure without validating the pointer, handling kernel and user targets uniformly. Only one, two, four and eight byte lengths are accepted, each staged through a same sized temporary before or after the accessor. Failure synthesizes protection fault information anchored at the target address, adding write indication for stores and user indication when the faulting context is unprivileged.

Emulated accesses run in a non sleepable atomic context where the fault handler avoids semaphore acquisition, so no extra fault enable or disable pairing is required. Bulk string operations are prohibited for these accesses because splitting them into separate read and write stages would re enter the same emulation path and nest without bound. Unsupported lengths trigger a one time warning and report an unsupported outcome rather than faulting.

Memory mapped input output emulation derives an address reference from decoded instruction and register state, rejects unresolvable references, translates the reference to a physical address, and augments fault information with a write marker when a store translation raises an exception. It then issues a hypervisor request whose operation distinguishes reads from writes, whose first parameter carries the physical address and whose second carries the byte count, with scratch space directed at a shared communication buffer.

Address reference derivation first ensures opcode acquisition and rejects null inputs, acquisition failure, or unrecognized address widths with a uniform invalid sentinel. Recognized two, four and eight byte widths each delegate to a dedicated width specific helper.

Sixteen bit linear address formation requires displacement acquisition and address width agreement, then obtains either a direct register value for register direct encodings or a ModRM derived effective value otherwise. Segment base and limit are resolved for the associated register offset, the masked effective value is checked against the limit, and the base is added. Virtual 8086 mode skips limit enforcement via an all ones limit and truncates the final linear value to twenty bits. Any resolution or bound failure yields an invalid sentinel.

Segment selection gives the instruction pointer a fixed resolution that ignores segments in 64-bit mode and selects code otherwise without inspecting override bytes. Other registers use default selection when string operations target the destination index or when no override is present, otherwise a single override byte determines the selection. Multiple overrides are rejected, missing base or empty limit are rejected, and long mode narrows overrides to FS and GS only.

Register identity derivation starts from a width dependent register file size that excludes eight upper registers when decoding non 64-bit code on 64-bit builds. Each query type extracts its selector from the appropriate addressing byte and adds eight when the corresponding extension flag is set. Displacement only base encodings and null scaled index encodings are rejected as domain errors, out of range identities warn once and fail, unknown query types log and fail, and valid identities translate to register block offsets.

Model specific register emulation discriminates read versus write by inspecting the second opcode byte for the read encoding and delegates to a shared handler. A helper maps the ModRM register memory field to a slot within the saved register block, returning null when unresolvable. Early exception forwarding restores the fault address control register for page faults, then forwards the trap number with the stored error code in the original accumulator slot.

Prefix scanning walks the stored prefix byte array in order until a zero terminator or the end of the storage, exposing each byte to the caller. Prefix attribute construction combines a prefix identifier with a fixed shift placement.
A local diagnostic alias forwards format text and arguments to the kernel logging facility.
